close_reason: Landed in 1491170 alongside JMAP-t307.9. Option (a) per bead: README clarification. 'union' → 'concatenation', explicit 'no dedup', plus the note that for plain-only messages where html_body mirrors text_body the same part_id appears twice. Same explanation in message_to_jmap_body rustdoc under a new 'body_value_part_ids shape' heading. PLAN.md item 6 rewritten — old wording claimed 'assumed disjoint' which was incorrect.
description:
JmapBodyFields.body_value_part_ids: Vec<String> (src/lib.rs:61) can
contain DUPLICATE part IDs. The construction at src/lib.rs:156-158
is plain concatenation, not union:

    let mut body_value_part_ids = Vec::with_capacity(
        msg.text_body.len() + msg.html_body.len()
    );
    body_value_part_ids.extend(msg.text_body.iter().cloned());
    body_value_part_ids.extend(msg.html_body.iter().cloned());

No dedup. For plain-text-only messages — by far the most common email
shape — RFC 8621 §4.1.4 mandates that htmlBody mirrors textBody, so
the same part ID appears in both lists, and body_value_part_ids ends
up with the same id twice. The existing test
message_to_jmap_body_plain_text_body (src/lib.rs:296-309) confirms
html_body.len() == 1 mirrors text_body.len() == 1 for plain-only
messages, which implies body_value_part_ids has length 2 with both
entries being the same string.

The newly-rewritten README (README.md:43) describes body_value_part_ids
as \"union of textBody and htmlBody part IDs\". The word \"union\"
implies set-semantics with dedup, which is NOT what the code does.
The accurate word is \"concatenation\". This is a contract bug in the
new doc text, not in the unchanged implementation.

What goes wrong for the caller:

The README's own \"How to use\" example (README.md:75-83) iterates
body_value_part_ids and calls decode_body_value for each entry, then
inserts into a HashMap:

    for part_id in &fields.body_value_part_ids {
        if let Some(part) = msg.part_index.find_by_id(part_id) {
            if let Ok(decoded) = decode_body_value(raw, part, Some(8192)) {
                body_values.insert(part_id.clone(), body_value_to_jmap(decoded));
            }
        }
    }

The HashMap insert silently dedups the result, but decode_body_value
runs TWICE on the duplicate part for plain-text emails. The cost is
wasted decoding work on the most common email shape — not a
correctness bug but a 2x CPU overhead in the steady-state path that
the maintainer is benchmarking in the new bench file.

A caller who, instead of HashMap, uses Vec<(String, EmailBodyValue)>
or a JSON-builder pattern that emits each entry directly to the wire,
would produce a JMAP bodyValues map with duplicate keys — at best a
size bloat, at worst a malformed response depending on how the JSON
encoder handles duplicate map keys.

Fix options (maintainer's choice):

  (a) README clarification: replace \"union\" with \"concatenation of\";
      add a one-sentence note that duplicates are expected for
      plain-only messages and the caller is responsible for dedup if
      their code path is order-sensitive or duplicate-sensitive.

  (b) Implementation change: dedup at construction time. Cheapest is
      to skip the second extend when text_body == html_body (the
      common mirror case); more general is to build through a
      BTreeSet<String> or use Vec::dedup after sorting. The
      maintainer should weigh whether preserving textBody-before-
      htmlBody order matters to callers.

Workspace context: PLAN.md item 6 (lines 174-178) anticipates this
case but mis-classifies it as \"text_body and html_body are assumed
disjoint\" — they are NOT disjoint by RFC 8621 design.
title: body_value_part_ids can contain duplicates; README calls it 'union'
